title: Suspended Days Standing Against a Workplace Cafe Management Program Contract Year
content:
Point one — the term in force. Where two or more standby charges stand on the contract in the twelve months up to the day the invoice is raised and ten or more suspended calendar days stand against the current contract year, the escalated fee is relieved in the share that those suspended calendar days bear to a thirty-day month, the figure so obtained rounded to the nearest cent; where fewer than two standby charges stand on the contract over those twelve months and ten or more suspended calendar days stand against the current contract year, the escalated fee is relieved in the share that the days falling within whole weeks of those suspended days bear to a thirty-day month, the figure so obtained rounded to the nearest cent; and where fewer than ten suspended calendar days stand against the current contract year, no suspended day relief is taken.

Point two — the two counts that decide. The first count is the standby charges standing on the contract in the twelve months up to the day the invoice is raised, judged at 2 or more against fewer than 2. The second count is the suspended calendar days standing against the current contract year on a contract held under the Workplace Cafe Management Program, judged at 10 or more against fewer than 10. The second count is decisive on its own: with fewer than 10 suspended calendar days against the current contract year, no suspended day relief is taken however many standby charges stand over those 12 months.

Point three — the share and what it is borne to. A thirty-day month is a month taken at 30 days. The share is the number of days the term names borne to those 30 days, that share is applied once to the escalated fee, and the figure so obtained is rounded to the nearest cent once.

Point four — days falling within whole weeks. Where fewer than 2 standby charges stand over those 12 months, the days counted into the share are not all of the suspended calendar days but the days falling within whole weeks of those suspended days, a whole week being 7 calendar days. Of 17 suspended calendar days, 14 fall within whole weeks; of 13, 7 do; of 6, none do.

Point five — the boundaries. Exactly 10 suspended calendar days standing against the current contract year are ten or more, and relief is taken; 9 are fewer than ten, and none is. Exactly 2 standby charges standing over those 12 months are two or more, and the suspended calendar days themselves are borne to a thirty-day month; 1 is fewer than two, and the days falling within whole weeks are borne instead.

Point six — worked on hypothetical records. Take a hypothetical escalated fee of 6200.00 USD and 17 suspended calendar days standing against the current contract year. With 3 standby charges over those 12 months, the share that 17 days bear to a thirty-day month, applied to 6200.00 USD, gives 3513.3333 USD to four decimal places, and the relief is 3513.33 USD. With 1 standby charge over those 12 months, the days falling within whole weeks of those 17 suspended days number 14, the share that 14 days bear to a thirty-day month applied to the same 6200.00 USD gives 2893.3333 USD to four decimal places, and the relief is 2893.33 USD. With 9 suspended calendar days standing against the current contract year, no suspended day relief is taken.
